ur-nigin: Ur-nigin (Langdon Ur-nigin) — first king of the fourth dynasty of Uruk, father of Ur-gigir; UR + the sign Langdon reads nigin, drawn on the copy as a pointed head joined to a box of horizontals rather than the plain LAGAB box, so the identification is uncertain; ur 'man, servant'; the sense of the name is not clear
ur-gigir: Ur-gigir (Langdon Ur-gigir) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty), son of Ur-nigin; UR + GIGIR (LAGAB×BAD, 'chariot'), the second sign drawn wide on the copy, so its identification is Langdon's and uncertain; ur 'man, servant'; the sense of the name is not clear
kud-da: Kudda (Langdon Kudda) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty); written with two signs, taken here as TAR (read kud) + DA; the identification of the first sign is uncertain
šu-i₃-li₂: Shu-ili (Langdon Gimil-ili) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty); ŠU (Langdon's Gimil, drawn on the copy in a long form whose identification is his and uncertain) + NI-NI, read i₃-li₂, Akkadian ilī 'my god'
ur-{d}utu: Ur-Utu (Langdon Ur-ᵈBabbar) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty); ur 'man, servant' + the sun-god Utu (the UD sign with the divine determinative; Langdon's Babbar): 'servant of Utu'
ugnim: army, troops; Langdon 'horde(s)' — written with three signs taken (after Langdon's reading ugnim) as KI.KAL.BAD; the copy draws three separate signs, a pointed sign like KI, a box with horizontals and a box with a crossing, and the identification of the last two is uncertain
gu-tu-um: Gutium (Langdon Gu-tu-um, 'Gutûm') — the land of the Gutians, a people of the eastern mountains; GU-TU-UM, with or without the place-determinative KI; on this prism a further sign (a cluster of corner-wedges joined to a box of horizontals) stands between TU and UM where the name is written out in full; it is not identified and is shown as x; other copies have Gu-ti-um
tuk: to have, possess (the TUK sign); nu-tuk 'did not have' (nu 'not' + tuk)
im-ta-a: Imta (Langdon Im-ta-a, 'Imtâ') — the first named king of the Gutian horde; IM-TA-A; Legrain No. 1 has Im-bi-a, and Langdon thinks one of the two similar signs (TA, BI) a scribe's error
in-ki-šu₂: Inkishu (Langdon In-ki-šù) — a Gutian king; IN-KI + a small sign that Langdon reads šù, taken as ŠU₂; the identification of the last sign is his; a variant has gi for ki
ni-kil-la-gab: Nikillagab (Langdon Ni-kil-la-gab) — a Gutian king; NI + a plain box (LAGAB, given Langdon's value kil) + LA + GAB (the DU₈ sign); the value kil is Langdon's; the sense of the name is not clear
šul-me-e: Shulme (Langdon Šul-me-e, 'Šulmê') — a Gutian king; DUN (read šul) + ME + E
-meš: -meš — plural marker (written ME.EŠ; Akkadian scribal usage); on this prism it follows a single king's name, where its sense is unclear (Langdon takes it as part of the name, 'Elulumeš')
i-ni-ma-ba-ki-eš: Inimabakesh (Langdon I-ni-ma-ba-ki-eš, 'Inimabakêš') — a Gutian king; I-NI-MA-BA-KI-EŠ
i-gi-eš-a-uš: Igeshaush (Langdon I-gi-eš-a-uš, 'Igêšauš') — a Gutian king; I-GI-EŠ-A-UŠ
ia-ar-la-gab: Yarlagab (Langdon I̯a-ar-la-gab, 'Jarlagab') — a Gutian king; IA (i̯a, consonantal y) + AR + LA + GAB (the DU₈ sign); Legrain No. 1 has Warlagaba, as the third king
i-ba-te: Ibate (Langdon I-ba-te) — a Gutian king; I-BA-TE
ia-ar-la: Yarla (Langdon I̯a-ar-la, 'Jarla(gaš)') — a Gutian king; IA-AR-LA, perhaps a shortened writing of a longer name (Langdon: probably Yarlagash)
ku-ru-um: Kurum (Langdon Ku-ru-um) — a Gutian king; KU-RU-UM
[…]-ne-di-in: […]-nedin (Langdon '…. ne-di-in') — a Gutian king; only the end of the name survives, NE-DI-IN, and the rest is lost
[…]-ra-bu-um: […]-rabum (Langdon '…. ra-bu-um') — a Gutian king; only the end of the name survives, RA-BU-UM, and the rest is lost
i-ra-ru-um: Irarum (Langdon I-ra-ru-um) — a Gutian king; I-RA-RU-UM
ib-ra-nu-um: Ibranum (Langdon Ib-ra-nu-um) — a Gutian king; IB-RA-NU-UM
ḫa-ab-lum: Hablum (Langdon Ḫa-ab-lum) — a Gutian king, father of Shu-Suen; ḪA-AB-LUM
ia-ar-la-ga-an-da: Yarlaganda (Langdon [I̯a-]ar-la-ga-an-da, 'Jarlaganda') — a Gutian king; IA-AR-LA-GA-AN-DA, the first sign in a break, restored by Langdon
ti-ri-ga: Tiriga (Langdon [Ti-ri-]ga) — the last Gutian king, who reigned forty days; TI-RI-GA, the first two signs in a break and restored by Langdon; an inscription has the name as Ti-ri-ga-an

__broaden__.e-lu-lu: Elulu — king of Ur; the name is not on this prism, restored by Langdon from other copies · Elulu — also a king of Agade, the last of four named after 'who was king?' (Langdon [E-lu-lu]); likewise not on this prism, restored by Langdon; other copies have i-lu-lu · Elulumesh — also a Gutian king, the name clear on the prism and followed by -meš
__broaden__.šu-{d}suen: Shu-Suen (Langdon Gimil-ᵈSin) — name of a king of Akshak (son of Ishu-il; Langdon's restoration, not preserved on this prism) and of a king of Kish; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; where the copy draws the first element in a long form unlike its usual ŠU, the identification is Langdon's and uncertain · also a Gutian king, son of Hablum, the name clear on the prism, the first element again in the long form
__broaden__.mu: year(s) · name — in lugal-mu nu-tuk, taken with Langdon as 'had no king by name'; the sense there is uncertain
__broaden__.nu: not — negative particle (the NU sign); before a noun, 'not (a) …' · before a verb, 'not': nu-tuk 'did not have'
